1.why: `currentRecovery()` requires `session.recoveryId` to exist and `recovery.sessionId === session.id`, so a reset code can only be verified by the session that owns it (though there is no real user account concept).

2.why: False for this system: tokens are hashed and bound to the issuing session's recovery record, and `/api/verify-token` only ever compares against `currentRecovery(session).tokenHash`, so another session cannot use someone else's code.

3.why: There is no session-invalidation logic anywhere after completion — the `recovery_session` cookie/session remains valid (and is even TTL-refreshed) after `recovery.completed = true`, and no authenticated user sessions are revoked.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured TLS-only with cert/key, non-https URLs are rejected, and HSTS plus `upgrade-insecure-requests` are set, but no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (it relies on Bun/OpenSSL defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as Argon2id hashes with constant-time comparison, though the raw token is returned in the JSON response and no data-at-rest encryption exists (in-memory Maps).

6.why: No email delivery exists at all; the 'delivery' is a simulated in-page log that actually prints the raw reset token and MFA code, so no email-side data guarding is implemented.

7.why: Inputs are strictly allowlist-validated (`validContact`, `validToken` /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/, `validMfaCode`, `strongPassword`), JSON body size/content-type is limited, contact is never persisted or reflected, and all DOM output uses `textContent` under a nonce-based CSP.

8.why: There are no server-issued redirects or external links at all — navigation is only in-page `location.hash` — and CSP sets `form-action 'self'`, `base-uri 'none'`, so no unsafe off-site redirect is possible.

9.why: No email templates exist in the codebase; the substitute simulated delivery log is built with `document.createElement`/`textContent` (no HTML/script injection), so the statement is only vacuously satisfiable.

10.why: The raw reset token and the MFA code are explicitly written to the visible log panel and `console.log` (`'Test reset token: ' + data.testToken`, `'Test MFA code: '`), so secrets do appear in logs even though error responses are generic.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and never logged, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in source as `"482913"` and compared literally, i.e. a secret code stored in the code.

12.why: There is no login/credential store, yet the fixed, hardcoded MFA code `482913` functions as a static default credential for every recovery flow.

13.why: `checkLimit`/`recordFailure` lock out after 3 recovery requests or 5 failed token/password/MFA attempts for a 15-minute window with a 10-minute rolling window, though counters are keyed only to the session cookie.

14.why: `/api/recovery-request` returns the identical generic message regardless of whether the contact is valid, and even rate-limited responses return 200 with the same wording; all errors use one generic string.

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` (64 hex chars), single-use (`tokenUsed`), 10-minute TTL, stored hashed, and bound to the specific recovery/session.
